title: The smoke that covers the people
translation: So watch for the day the sky brings a visible smoke, covering the people: this is a painful punishment.
body: As **haze from Indonesia's fires** cancels flights between KL and Singapore, read this verse. Early Muslims already disagreed on it. **Ibn Mas'ud** said it described a past famine in Mecca, when hunger made the sky look like smoke. Others read it as a **sign of the end times**, like Joel's “pillars of smoke” in the Bible.
question: Verse 15 says the punishment will be lifted “a little”. Does that fit a past event or the end of time better?
source_label: Al Jazeera, 13 Oct 2026 · Sahih al-Bukhari, tafsir of Surah 44
reading: Nicolai Sinai, The Qur'an: A Historical-Critical Introduction (2017)
